## Script Summary 
- Filters probes (CpG sites) in each SummarizedExperiment object (TCGA project) 

- Creates a histogram plot showing the # of probes removed at each filtering step

- Saves processed SummarizedExperiments

## Data Loading
Load in SummarizedExperiment RDS objects and define output directory
```{r data loading}
#Path where the summarized experiment objects you are updating are located
se_directory <- file.path(TCGA, "methylation/processed_data/all/")

#Path to directory you want to output to
output_directory <- file.path(PATH, "data/methylation/processed_SummarizedExperiments")
plot_path <- file.path(PATH,"data/methylation/preprocessing_plots")
```

Here we load in a single TCGA project (BRCA) to show the workflow
```{r Load in BRCA object}
BRCA_methyl <- readRDS(file.path(TCGA,"methylation/processed_data/all/TCGA-BRCA_methylation.rds"))
```

## Probe Filtering
These are the preprocessing steps taken to remove poor performing probes (CpG sites)
that may influence downstream analysis. There is no consensus preprocessing steps, so I performed
the ones that appeared most often in literature. 

Note that we are starting from BETA values (level 3 methylation data) that has already 
undergone some preprocessing using the Sesame pipeline: 

Link to GDC's explanation of methylation processing
( https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/Bioinformatics_Pipelines/Methylation_Pipeline/)

Here we remove (per TCGA project):
  All NA Probes: These probes are missing all of their values, most likely due to 
  low detection p-value calculated during Sesame workflow
  
  Non-CpG probes: This is a common preprocessing step to remove probes targeting 
  sites that are not "CpG", usually called "ch" as it indicates a C followed by either A,T, or C. 
  
  Probes that Overlap with SNPs: SNPs can affect probe binding and methylation readings. 
  We remove both "common" SNPs and those with a minor allele frequency greater than 1%. This is determined
  using the MASK annotations (see next) from a 2017 paper. 

  General Mask Probes: This step helps in removing probes flagged for various issues, 
  adding another layer of quality control. This is generated from a 2017 study (https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkw967) which
  created all MASK annotations through testing which CpGs methylation levels are heavily affected by SNPs, repetitive regions,
  etc. 
  
  Probes with more than 20% missing values: Setting a threshold (like 20%) for 
  missing values is standard practice. If a probe has more than 20% of its value 
  missing across samples, drop it
  
  Cross-Reactive probes: Probes that have been proven to bind to multiple sequences
  We use "maxprobe" here which combines results from two papers identifying cross
  reactive probes :  https://github.com/markgene/maxprobes

  Removing Probes on Sex Chromosomes: Relevant if sex chromosome-related variations 
  are not the focus of your study. Sex chromosome probes perform poorly and are 
  difficult to account for when analyzing both genders. 

```{r Removing bad Cpg sites}
 filter_probes <- function(summarized_experiment) {
    initial_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(summarized_experiment))[1]
    cat("Number of CpG probes initially: ", initial_count, "\n")
    
    # Remove rows with all NAs
    rows_with_all_na <- rowSums(!is.na(SummarizedExperiment::assay(summarized_experiment))) == 0
    methyl_subset <- summarized_experiment[!rows_with_all_na, ]
    post_na_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    cat("Number of ALL NA CpG probes removed: ", initial_count - post_na_count, "\n")
    
    # Remove non-CpG probes
    methyl_subset <- methyl_subset[SummarizedExperiment::rowData(methyl_subset)$probeType != "ch", ]
    post_nonCpG_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    cat("Number of non-CpG probes removed: ", post_na_count - post_nonCpG_count, "\n")
    
    # Remove probes that overlap with SNPs (at least 1% MAF in any population)
    methyl_subset <- methyl_subset[!SummarizedExperiment::rowData(methyl_subset)$MASK_snp5_common, ]
    post_snp_common_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    cat("Number of common SNP probes removed: ", post_nonCpG_count - post_snp_common_count, "\n")
    
    # Remove any probes that have a GLOBAL minor allele freq >1%
    methyl_subset <- methyl_subset[!SummarizedExperiment::rowData(methyl_subset)$MASK_snp5_GMAF1p, ]
    post_snp_GMAF1_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    cat("Number of probes with SNPS MAF >1% removed: ", post_snp_common_count - post_snp_GMAF1_count, "\n")
    
    # Remove any probes that are flagged with MASK_general
    # This is a combination of multiple flags indicating a problematic probe
    # Usually only all NA probes are flagged (should already be removed)
    methyl_subset <- methyl_subset[!SummarizedExperiment::rowData(methyl_subset)$MASK_general, ]
    post_mask_gen_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    cat("Number of flagged probes removed: ", post_snp_GMAF1_count - post_mask_gen_count, "\n")
    
    # Calculate the proportion of missing values for each probe in the subset
    proportion_missing <- apply(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset), 1, function(x) sum(is.na(x)) / length(x))
    # Identify probes with more than 20% missing values
    probes_to_remove <- which(proportion_missing > 0.20)
    # Remove these probes from the subset
    methyl_subset <- methyl_subset[-probes_to_remove, ]
    post_gt20missing_probe_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    cat("Number of probes with >20% missing values removed: ", post_mask_gen_count - post_gt20missing_probe_count, "\n")
    
    # Finally remove cross reactive probes (from the maxprobes library)
    xloci <- maxprobes::xreactive_probes(array_type = "450K")
    rows_to_keep <- !rownames(methyl_subset) %in% xloci
    methyl_subset <- methyl_subset[rows_to_keep, ]
    post_crossreactive_probe_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    cat("Number of cross reactive probes removed: ", post_gt20missing_probe_count - post_crossreactive_probe_count, "\n")
    
    # Remove any probes that are on sex chromosomes (X and Y)
    methyl_filtered <- methyl_subset[!SummarizedExperiment::rowData(methyl_subset)$chrm_A %in% c("chrX", "chrY"), ]
    final_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_filtered))[1]
    cat("Number of sex chromosome probes removed: ", post_crossreactive_probe_count - final_count, "\n")
    
    cat("Number of CpG sites after all filtering: ", final_count, "\n")
    
    # Return list of results
    list(
        filtered_data = methyl_filtered, 
        initial_count = initial_count, 
        final_count = final_count,
        post_na_count = post_na_count,
        post_nonCpG_count = post_nonCpG_count,
        post_snp_common_count = post_snp_common_count,
        post_snp_GMAF1_count = post_snp_GMAF1_count,
        post_mask_gen_count = post_mask_gen_count,
        post_gt20missing_probe_count = post_gt20missing_probe_count,
        post_crossreactive_probe_count = post_crossreactive_probe_count
    )
}

methyl_filtered <- filter_probes(BRCA_methyl)

BRCA_methyl_filtered <- methyl_filtered$filtered_data
# Check that the metadata associated with a randomly selected probe is the same after filtering
cat("Randomly Selected probe metadata is the same after filtering: ", 
    identical(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(BRCA_methyl_filtered)["cg16619049", ], 
              SummarizedExperiment::rowData(BRCA_methyl)["cg16619049", ]))

cat("Randomly Selected probe methylation values are the same after filtering: ", 
    identical(SummarizedExperiment::assay(BRCA_methyl_filtered)["cg16619049", ], 
              SummarizedExperiment::assay(BRCA_methyl)["cg16619049", ]))

```

## Filtering Visualization
Here, we plot the number of probes (CpG sites) removed during each step of the
filtering process. 

Its important to note this calculates the number of probes removed at each STEP, 
not necessarily the number of original probes that would be dropped from filtering 
the category. 

For example, in the BRCA project we had 8657 probes removed for having >20%
missing values. This occurs after the removal of the ALL NA probes, and thus does
not represent the # of probes with >20% missing values but just the remaining probes
at the step of the filtering. 

Likewise, there are roughly 39,000 cross reactive probes but only the remaining cross reactive
probes are removed by that filtering step (2784), meaning the remaining were already removed

```{r Plot of filtered probes}
plot_removed_probes <- function(filtered_data) {
    # Extract counts from the filtered_data list
    initial_count <- filtered_data$initial_count
    post_na_count <- filtered_data$post_na_count
    post_nonCpG_count <- filtered_data$post_nonCpG_count
    post_snp_common_count <- filtered_data$post_snp_common_count
    post_snp_GMAF1_count <- filtered_data$post_snp_GMAF1_count
    post_mask_gen_count <- filtered_data$post_mask_gen_count
    post_gt20missing_probe_count <- filtered_data$post_gt20missing_probe_count
    post_crossreactive_probe_count <- filtered_data$post_crossreactive_probe_count
    final_count <- filtered_data$final_count

    removed_counts <- c(
        initial_count - post_na_count,
        post_na_count - post_nonCpG_count,
        post_nonCpG_count - post_snp_common_count,
        post_snp_common_count - post_snp_GMAF1_count,
        post_snp_GMAF1_count - post_mask_gen_count,
        post_mask_gen_count - post_gt20missing_probe_count,
        post_gt20missing_probe_count - post_crossreactive_probe_count,
        post_crossreactive_probe_count - final_count
    )

    data_to_plot <- data.frame(
        Step = c("All NAs", "Non-CpG", "SNP Common", "SNP GMAF>1%", "MASK_general", ">20% Missing Values", "Cross-reactive probes", "ChrX/Y"),
        Probes_Removed = removed_counts
    )

    # Sort data from largest to smallest number of probes removed
    data_to_plot <- data_to_plot[order(-data_to_plot$Probes_Removed),]

    # Create the plot
    ggplot2::ggplot(data_to_plot, ggplot2::aes(x = reorder(Step, -Probes_Removed), y = Probes_Removed, fill = Step)) +
        ggplot2::geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
        ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = Probes_Removed), vjust = -0.3, color = "black", size = 3.5) +
        ggplot2::scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") +
        ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
        ggplot2::labs(title = "Number of Probes Removed at Each Filtering Step", 
             x = "Filtering Step", y = "Number of Probes Removed") +
        ggplot2::theme(legend.title = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") + 
        ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) # Rotate x-axis labels
}

# Example usage
plot_removed_probes(methyl_filtered)

```

## Comment on Normalization
The TCGA DNA methylation data (level 3 beta values) were processed using the Sesame pipeline, 
which is  designed to  reduce both inter- and intra-array technical variations, 
including probe type biases and batch effects. Given the comprehensive preprocessing by Sesame,  
additional normalization should not be necessary at this step.

Papers that start from the level 3 beta values do not mention any normalization steps. 

```{r Normalization check}
# Function to plot beta-value distributions for different probe types with random sampling
plot_beta_distributions_by_type_sampled <- function(methyl_data, sample_size = 10000) {
  # Extract beta values
  beta_values <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_data)

  # Extract probe types from rowData
  probe_types <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(methyl_data)$designType

  # Randomly sample probes
  sampled_indices <- sample(nrow(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_data)), sample_size)

  # Filter beta values and probe types based on sampled indices
  sampled_beta_values <- beta_values[sampled_indices, ]
  sampled_probe_types <- probe_types[sampled_indices]
  
  # Convert to long format
  sampled_beta_values_long <- reshape2::melt(sampled_beta_values)
  sampled_beta_values_long$Type <- sampled_probe_types

  # Ensure there are at least two types before plotting
  if (length(unique(sampled_beta_values_long$Type)) < 2) {
    stop("Not enough probe types for comparison. Please check your data.")
  }

  # Plot distributions
  ggplot2::ggplot(sampled_beta_values_long, ggplot2::aes(x = value, fill = Type)) +
    ggplot2::geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "Sampled Beta Value Distributions by Probe Type",
         x = "Beta Value", y = "Density",
         fill = "Probe Type") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +  # Use a specific palette
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
}

# Example usage with a sample size of 100,000 probes
plot_beta_distributions_by_type_sampled(BRCA_methyl_filtered, sample_size = 100000)

```

## M-Values versus Beta-Values
Here we plot the distributions of the beta values and M-values. 
```{r}
set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility

# Extract M-values and Beta-values
m_values <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(BRCA_methyl_filtered, "M-values")
b_values <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(BRCA_methyl_filtered, "Beta-values")

# Sample M-values
sampled_m_values <- m_values[sample(nrow(m_values), 10000), ]
sampled_m_values_long <- reshape2::melt(sampled_m_values, na.rm = TRUE, value.name = "M_value")

# Plot M-values
ggplot2::ggplot(sampled_m_values_long, ggplot2::aes(x = M_value)) +
    ggplot2::geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "Distribution of Sampled M-values", x = "M-value", y = "Frequency")

# Sample Beta-values
sampled_b_values <- b_values[sample(nrow(b_values), 10000), ]
sampled_b_values_long <- reshape2::melt(sampled_b_values, na.rm = TRUE, value.name = "Beta_value")

# Plot Beta-values
ggplot2::ggplot(sampled_b_values_long, ggplot2::aes(x = Beta_value)) +
    ggplot2::geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "red", color = "black") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "Distribution of Sampled Beta-values", x = "Beta-value", y = "Frequency")

```



## Apply Filtering to all TCGA projects
Here we apply the two defined functions to all TCGA projects to perform filtering.
  - Filter probes
  - Calculate M-Values and add them as a second assay in Summarized Experiment Object

Note: A different number of probes are removed from each project. 

This code block outputs the now filtered SummarizedExperiment objects to the following directory
- /restricted/projectnb/agedisease/projects/pancancer_aging_pbock/data/methylation/processed_SummarizedExperiments

and the histogram visualization of removed probes to: 
- /restricted/projectnb/agedisease/projects/pancancer_aging_pbock/data/methylation/preprocessing_plots

```{r filter SEs}
# Creates a list of all files ending in .rds in se_directory
file_list <- list.files(path = se_directory, pattern = "*.rds", full.names = TRUE)

# Loop through each file
for (file_path in file_list) {
    cat("Filtering and saving ", file_path)
  
    # Read the SummarizedExperiment object
    se_obj <- readRDS(file_path)

    # Apply filter_probes function
    filtered_result <- filter_probes(se_obj)

    # Define new file names for the output
    file_name <- basename(file_path)
    new_file_path <- file.path(output_directory, file_name)
    plot_file_path <- file.path(plot_path, sub("\\.rds$", "_FilteringSummary.png", file_name))
    
    # Add M-values and save SummarizedExperiment object
    new_se <- filtered_result$filtered_data
    #new_se <- calc_mvals(new_se)
    saveRDS(new_se, new_file_path)

    # Generate and save the plot
    ggplot2::ggsave(plot_file_path, plot = plot_removed_probes(filtered_result), width = 10, height = 8)
}
```
